defmodule Rocola.Spotify do
  @moduledoc """
  The only way the rest of the app talks to Spotify. Callers use these functions;
  they delegate to the adapter set in `config :rocola, :spotify`
  (`Rocola.Spotify.Fake` by default, `Rocola.Spotify.Web` later).

  A new capability = a new callback here + `Fake` implementation + `Web` stub.
  """

  @type track :: %{
          uri: String.t(),
          name: String.t(),
          artist: String.t(),
          duration_ms: pos_integer()
        }
  @type device :: %{
          id: String.t(),
          name: String.t(),
          is_active: boolean(),
          is_restricted: boolean()
        }

  @callback search(query :: String.t()) :: {:ok, [track]} | {:error, term}
  @callback devices() :: {:ok, [device]} | {:error, term}
  @callback transfer_playback(device_id :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term}
  # Add-only: Spotify's API can append to the queue but never remove or reorder.
  @callback add_to_queue(uri :: String.t()) :: :ok | {:error, term}
  @callback queue() :: {:ok, [track]} | {:error, term}
  @callback now_playing() :: {:ok, track | nil} | {:error, term}

  defp adapter, do: Application.fetch_env!(:rocola, :spotify)

  def search(q), do: adapter().search(q)
  def devices, do: adapter().devices()
  def transfer_playback(id), do: adapter().transfer_playback(id)
  def add_to_queue(uri), do: adapter().add_to_queue(uri)
  def queue, do: adapter().queue()
  def now_playing, do: adapter().now_playing()
end
defmodule RocolaWeb.Router do
  use RocolaWeb, :router

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {RocolaWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development
  if Application.compile_env(:rocola, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

name: spotify-web-api
description: Rocola's Spotify know-how. Use when adding or changing anything that searches songs, lists devices, queues or skips tracks, or shows now-playing, including the Rocola.Spotify behaviour and its Fake and Web adapters. Not for UI-only styling, renames or non-Spotify work.

# Spotify in Rocola

All Spotify access goes through the `Rocola.Spotify` behaviour (`lib/rocola/spotify.ex`).
Adapters: `Fake` (dev/test default, no token) and `Web` (real API, stub). Never call an adapter directly.

## Recipe for a new Spotify capability
1. Add a `@callback` and a delegating function in `Rocola.Spotify`.
2. Implement it in `Fake` AND stub it in `Web` (`{:error, :not_implemented}`), same change.
3. Put queue/limit/vote rules in `Rocola.Jukebox`, never in the adapter.
4. LiveViews call `Rocola.Jukebox`/`Rocola.Spotify`, never `Req` or `Repo`.
5. Tests use the Fake (`Rocola.Spotify.Fake.reset/0` in `setup`), never the network.
6. `mix precommit` must pass.

## Real API rules the Fake must mirror
- The queue is add-only: no remove, no reorder. Skips, votes and per-guest limits live in Rocola's own
  SQLite queue; send Spotify one song ahead. Never add a "remove from queue" callback.
- Playback commands need Premium and an active device. Devices only appear while awake.
- Devices with `is_restricted: true` are shown unavailable and never get commands.
- Success is often `204 No Content` with no body: don't pattern-match on a body.
- `429` carries a `Retry-After` header (seconds): wait that long, then retry once.
- There is no push for track changes: poll `now_playing` (or broadcast over PubSub from the context that owns playback).

## Real adapter (later)
Authorization Code flow; access token refreshed only by `Rocola.Spotify.TokenServer`; never log or store
tokens elsewhere. Scopes: `user-read-playback-state`, `user-modify-playback-state`,
`user-read-currently-playing`. Endpoint details: `reference/endpoints.md`.
3:  In-memory Spotify for dev and test: ~50 seeded songs, 2 devices (one `is_restricted`),
4:  and simulated playback. Mirrors real API limits: add-only queue, restricted devices
5-  reject commands, playback needs an active device. No network, no token.
6-  """

14-             %{

16-               name: "#{w} #{a}",

      case Enum.find(s.devices, &(&1.id == id)) do

defmodule RocolaWeb.PageControllerTest do
  use RocolaWeb.ConnCase

  test "GET /", %{conn: conn} do
    conn = get(conn, ~p"/")
    assert html_response(conn, 200) =~ "Peace of mind from prototype to production"
  end
end
# 001: Architecture

## Decisions
- **Spotify behind a behaviour.** `Rocola.Spotify` defines the callbacks; `Fake` (default in dev/test)
  and `Web` (real API + `TokenServer`, stub) implement them. Switching is config plus credentials.
  Why: build and test with no account, token or network.
- **Own queue.** Spotify's API can add to its queue but not remove or reorder, so Rocola keeps its
  queue in SQLite (skips, votes, per-guest limits) and feeds Spotify one song ahead.
- **Fake mirrors real limits** (add-only queue, restricted devices, active device required) so
  behaviour proven against it carries over to the real adapter.
- **Stack:** Phoenix LiveView, SQLite (`ecto_sqlite3`), `mix release` for aarch64 on a Raspberry Pi.
- **Tidewave** (dev only) gives the coding agent access to the running app over MCP.

Playback devices

{@error}

No devices found. Wake one up and refresh.

  • {d.name} Active Unavailable
""" end end

defmodule RocolaWeb.AdminLiveTest do
  use RocolaWeb.ConnCase
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  setup do
    Rocola.Spotify.Fake.reset()
    :ok
  end

  test "restricted device is unavailable and cannot be selected", %{conn: conn} do
    {:ok, view, html} = live(conn, ~p"/admin")
    assert html =~ "Living Room"
    assert has_element?(view, "#device-fake-locked", "Unavailable")
    refute has_element?(view, "#device-fake-locked button")

    # forged event is rejected and nothing becomes active
    render_click(view, "select", %{"id" => "fake-locked"})
    assert {:ok, devs} = Rocola.Spotify.devices()
    refute Enum.any?(devs, & &1.is_active)
  end

  test "select available device and refresh", %{conn: conn} do
    {:ok, view, _} = live(conn, ~p"/admin")
    view |> element("#device-fake-living-room button") |> render_click()
    assert render(view) =~ "Active"
    assert render_click(element(view, "#refresh")) =~ "Living Room"
  end
end

defmodule RocolaWeb.Router do
  use RocolaWeb, :router

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {RocolaWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", RocolaWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", RocolaWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard in development
  if Application.compile_env(:rocola, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: RocolaWeb.Telemetry
    end
  end
end

`/admin` now lists the playback devices, and `mix precommit` ends with 11 tests passing, including two new ones for this page.

- **Refresh:** a button re-fetches the device list.
- **Restricted devices:** they show an "Unavailable" badge, are dimmed, and have no Select button. I also check on the server that the device isn't restricted before sending a command, so a hand-crafted select event for one is rejected with a flash error.
- **Select button:** you didn't ask for one, but "selectable" implied it, so I added it for available devices. It calls `Rocola.Spotify.transfer_playback` and shows an "Active" badge on the chosen device.
- **Tests:** `test/rocola_web/live/admin_live_test.exs` covers the unavailable device, a forged select, a normal select, and refresh.
- **Files:** the page is `lib/rocola_web/live/admin_live.ex`, with a `live "/admin"` route in `lib/rocola_web/router.ex`.

I only saw the last lines of the precommit output, so I didn't see its exit code. It also logged a one-off "database is locked" error from the SQLite connection, which didn't stop the tests from running.

I left out admin authentication, since you didn't ask for it. `/admin` is open to anyone who can reach the Pi, so add a login before exposing it beyond your home network.
